changes.description: Property allowed_payment_method_types added to schema checkout.session.
changes.migration_hint:
Removes the payment_method_types parameter from the create Checkout Session method. You can no longer pass `payment_method_types` when you create a Checkout Session. Use dynamic payment methods to manage payment methods from the Dashboard without writing code.

You can also use excluded_payment_method_types to exclude specific payment methods from the dynamic payment methods results or the new allowed_payment_method_types parameter to specify a set of payment methods.

The allowed_payment_method_types  parameter accepts an array of payment method type and filters the list to only compatible payment methods based on other parameters such as `currency`, `amount`, and `customer`. The compatible subset is shown in the payment_method_types property of the response.

Previously, payment_method_types returned an error when you specified an incompatible payment method. `allowed_payment_method_types` silently filters out incompatible methods and returns only those that work with the current configuration.

Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive/2026-09-30/remove-payment-method-types-checkout-sessions

changes.description: Property status_details added to schema invoice.
changes.migration_hint:
Adds a new status_details property to Invoices. When an invoice has a status of `uncollectible` and a supported reason is available, the status_details.uncollectible.reason property indicates why the invoice became uncollectible. This open enum has the following values:

- `max_payment_attempts`: The maximum number of payment attempts was reached.
- `payment_not_received`: Payment wasn’t received for the invoice.
- `subscription_canceled`: The subscription associated with the invoice was canceled.
- `subscription_paused`: The subscription associated with the invoice had `pause_collection` set.
- `user_forgiven`: The invoice was marked uncollectible by the user.

We only include `status_details` when the invoice’s `status` is `uncollectible`. The new `status_details` property is separate from the existing status_transitions property, which contains timestamps at which the invoice status was updated.

Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive/2026-09-30/invoice-uncollectible-status-detail

changes.description: Property current_trial added to schema subscription_item.
changes.migration_hint:
Adds generally available Trial Offers for subscriptions. Previously, a subscription used a single trial period for the entire subscription. Trial Offers let you define reusable free or paid introductory pricing for individual subscription items, each with its own price and billing period.

A Trial Offer specifies the recurring price to charge during the trial, the number of billing intervals that the trial lasts, and the post-trial price to use when the trial ends. Because Trial Offers define the trial price, they support both free and paid trialing periods. When the trial ends, we automatically change the subscription item to the configured post-trial price.

You can apply a trial offer when you create a subscription, add one to an existing subscription item, or replace an item’s existing trial offer. A subscription can contain both trial and non-trial items, each with its own price and billing period. This lets you offer a trial for an add-on or premium product without changing the billing behavior of the subscription’s other items.

Trial offers are reusable across multiple subscriptions. You can’t change their pricing and duration after creation, so archiving an offer prevents it from being used for new subscription items without affecting trials that are already in progress.

At trial end, you can configure whether Stripe sends an invoice, cancels, or pauses the subscription if the customer has no payment method. You can also configure whether the subscription’s billing cycle anchor resets when a trial offer ends.

Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive/2026-09-30/trial-offer-ga

Adds support for BLIK recurring off-session payments in Poland. You can accept recurring off-session BLIK charges by creating Mandates with your customers.

This release adds the following BLIK functionality:

- Accounts v1 support for the blik_recurring_payments capability.
- Accounts v2 support for blik_recurring_payments in:
  - The merchant capabilities configuration
  - requirements and future requirements entries that restrict capabilities
  - Merchant capability status updates.
- PaymentIntents, SetupIntents, and Checkout Sessions now include a mandate_options parameter in BLIK payment method options.
- PaymentIntents now include off_session as a value for setup_future_usage in BLIK payment method options.
- SetupIntents now include a blik payment method options parameter.
- Mandates now include BLIK payment_method_details including the expires_at and type properties.
- Checkout Sessions now include BLIK payment method options on setup_intent_data and subscription_data
- BLIK descriptions for Subscriptions, Invoices, Customers, and Quotes now reflect support for automatic charge collection.

Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive/2026-09-30/blik-recurring-off-session-payments

changes.migration_hint:
Adds generally available Trial Offers for subscriptions. Previously, a subscription used a single trial period for the entire subscription. Trial Offers let you define reusable free or paid introductory pricing for individual subscription items, each with its own price and billing period.

A Trial Offer specifies the recurring price to charge during the trial, the number of billing intervals that the trial lasts, and the post-trial price to use when the trial ends. Because Trial Offers define the trial price, they support both free and paid trialing periods. When the trial ends, we automatically change the subscription item to the configured post-trial price.

You can apply a trial offer when you create a subscription, add one to an existing subscription item, or replace an item’s existing trial offer. A subscription can contain both trial and non-trial items, each with its own price and billing period. This lets you offer a trial for an add-on or premium product without changing the billing behavior of the subscription’s other items.

Trial offers are reusable across multiple subscriptions. You can’t change their pricing and duration after creation, so archiving an offer prevents it from being used for new subscription items without affecting trials that are already in progress.

At trial end, you can configure whether Stripe sends an invoice, cancels, or pauses the subscription if the customer has no payment method. You can also configure whether the subscription’s billing cycle anchor resets when a trial offer ends.

Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive/2026-09-30/trial-offer-ga

A subscription can contain both trial and non-trial items, each with its own price and billing period. This lets you offer a trial for an add-on or premium product without changing the billing behavior of the subscription’s other items.

Trial offers are reusable across multiple subscriptions. You can’t change their pricing and duration after creation, so archiving an offer prevents it from being used for new subscription items without affecting trials that are already in progress.

At trial end, you can configure whether Stripe sends an invoice, cancels, or pauses the subscription if the customer has no payment method. You can also configure whether the subscription’s billing cycle anchor resets when a trial offer ends.

changes.description: Property configuration.merchant.capabilities.blik_recurring_payments added to POST /v2/core/accounts/{id}.
changes.migration_hint:
Adds support for BLIK recurring off-session payments in Poland. You can accept recurring off-session BLIK charges by creating Mandates with your customers.

This release adds the following BLIK functionality:

- Accounts v1 support for the blik_recurring_payments capability.
- Accounts v2 support for blik_recurring_payments in:
  - The merchant capabilities configuration
  - requirements and future requirements entries that restrict capabilities
  - Merchant capability status updates.
- PaymentIntents, SetupIntents, and Checkout Sessions now include a mandate_options parameter in BLIK payment method options.
- PaymentIntents now include off_session as a value for setup_future_usage in BLIK payment method options.
- SetupIntents now include a blik payment method options parameter.
- Mandates now include BLIK payment_method_details including the expires_at and type properties.
- Checkout Sessions now include BLIK payment method options on setup_intent_data and subscription_data
- BLIK descriptions for Subscriptions, Invoices, Customers, and Quotes now reflect support for automatic charge collection.

Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive/2026-09-30/blik-recurring-off-session-payments

changes.description: Property configuration.merchant.capabilities.satispay_payments added to POST /v2/core/accounts/{id}.
changes.migration_hint:
Adds satispay_payments as a new capability under configuration.merchant.capabilities on Accounts v2. You can request this capability when you create or update a v2 Account by setting `satispay_payments.requested` to `true`. The capability includes a status property that reports whether Satispay payments are active, pending, restricted, or unsupported for the account, along with a status_details array that provides additional context.

Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive/2026-09-30/satispay-payments-capability-for-accounts-v2-api

changes.migration_hint:
The sepa_debit_payments.creditor_id property on Accounts now returns Stripe’s country-specific shared SEPA Creditor Identifier) when an account doesn’t have a custom one. Previously, this property was omitted for accounts using the shared identifier.

You can now set a custom SEPA Creditor Identifier to be used for SEPA Direct Debit payments when you create a v1 Account. In Accounts v2, you can set a custom SEPA Creditor Identifier when you create or update a v2 Account using the configuration.merchant.sepa_debit_payments.creditor_id parameter.
